_comment: Declarative deployment-dependency rules for deploy/ops/validate-deployment.py. Each rule says: WHEN a service declares a capability (a truthy flag / an env value / merely existing), it must REQUIRE the config that capability depends on — env vars, bind mounts, secrets, and config files. Adding a future check = adding a rule here (no code change). Categories covered: required-env, required-mount, feature-flag, secret, config-file. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md -> Deployment-dependency validation.

rules.why: RWE_FEED_POLL=1 starts the engine's in-process RSS poller, which resolves its feed list from RWE_RSS_FEEDS and reads the mounted feed file. Without both, rss_ingest.load_feeds() returns 0 feeds and the poller silently ingests nothing while appearing healthy (prod incident 2026-07-21).
rules.fix: On the `api` service add `RWE_RSS_FEEDS: /app/feeds/rss_feeds.txt` and the bind-mount `./rss_feeds.example.txt:/app/feeds/rss_feeds.txt:ro` — in the AWS override too, because its `volumes: !override` replaces the list.

rules.why: In production the engine fail-closes: it refuses per-user calls without RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET and refuses to boot if it is unset. It must be wired from deploy/.env (interpolated), never hardcoded into the compose file.
rules.fix: On the `api` service set `RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET:?set RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET in deploy/.env}`.

rules.why: The web tier signs engine calls with the same shared secret; it must be present, match the engine's, and be supplied from deploy/.env.
rules.fix: On the `web` service set `RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${RWE_INTERNAL_SECRET:?...}` (identical to the engine).

rules.why: Google OAuth is the only production sign-in method; web/instrumentation.ts validates these at startup and process.exit(1)s if any is missing, so the web tier would crash-loop.
rules.fix: On the `web` service wire NEXTAUTH_URL + the three OAuth secrets from deploy/.env (`${NEXTAUTH_SECRET:?...}` etc.).

rules.why: Caddy is the only internet-facing process; it terminates TLS and reverse-proxies using the mounted Caddyfile. Without that config file mounted, the edge serves nothing.
rules.fix: On the `caddy` service keep the mount `./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro`.

rules.why: The engine's SQLite database and local backups live under /app/data; without the mount the DB would be created on the ephemeral container layer and lost on every recreation.
rules.fix: On the `api` service keep a volume mounted at /app/data (named volume in dev, host bind-mount in prod).
